rounds.text: Hazoor Multi Projects Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive price-to-book ratio of 0.60x against a book value of ₹ 23.6 [E2], and at a steep discount to its sector benchmarks in both P/E and EV/EBITDA [E6, E11]. Fundamental performance shows explosive operational momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 71% [E15], a TTM operating margin surging to 66% [E22], and a remarkable quarterly operating margin of 81% in September 2026 [E23]. This profitability is backed by strong cash generation, demonstrating a stellar cash conversion ratio of 2.26x with ₹ 97 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 [E26, E27]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is swelling, evidenced by foreign institutional holdings climbing to 26.79% alongside positive money flow [E34, E36], while a discounted cash flow model suggests a massive margin of safety with the market price pricing in negative growth [E38, E39]. Conceded: promoter holdings have declined to 13.70% [E33], free cash flow was negative at Rs -282 Cr [E28], and compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -20% [E14].

Hazoor Multi Projects Ltd carries substantial structural and financial risks that undermine its seemingly low valuation. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months stands at a concerning -20% [E14], signaling a contraction in top-line demand despite recent profit spikes. Furthermore, the company suffers from severe cash burn, reporting a devastating free cash flow of Rs -282 Cr in March 2026 [E28] alongside rising borrowings of Rs 478 Cr in September 2026 [E31]. This cash drain is compounded by ballooning working capital requirements, with working capital days expanding drastically from 304 days to 470 days [E48]. Governance and skin-in-the-game are equally alarming, as promoter holdings have plummeted by 12.2 percentage points since December 2023 down to a meager 13.70% [E33], flagged explicitly as a negative low promoter holding [E44]. Adding to the balance sheet fragility, the company carries massive contingent liabilities of Rs 415 Cr [E46]. Conceded: the company exhibits a low price-to-book ratio of 0.60x [E2], strong operating cash flow of Rs 97 Cr for March 2026 [E27], and an attractive DCF margin of safety [E38].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -20% [E14], working capital days have increased to 470 days [E48], borrowings rose to Rs 478 Cr [E31], contingent liabilities are Rs 415 Cr [E46], and promoter holdings decreased to 13.70% [E33]. However, the contraction in top-line sales has not impaired profitability, as compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months surges at 71% [E15], backed by a massive operating margin of 66% in TTM and 81% in September 2026 [E22, E23]. While free cash flow reached Rs -282 Cr [E28], operating cash flow remains robust at Rs 97 Cr for March 2026 [E27], with cash conversion at an impressive 2.26x indicating profits are fully backed by cash [E26]. The low promoter holding is strongly counterbalanced by rising foreign institutional participation, which expanded to 26.79% alongside positive institutional money flow [E34, E36]. Finally, the market drastically under-appreciates these improving fundamentals by pricing the stock at just 0.60x book value [E2] and offering a massive 58.4% margin of safety against intrinsic value [E38].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months surges at 71% [E15], and operating cash flow reached Rs 97 Cr in March 2026 [E27]. However, the bull's reliance on high margins masks severe capital destruction, evidenced by a massive free cash flow burn of Rs -282 Cr [E28] and ballooning working capital requirements that stretched from 304 days to an alarming 470 days [E48]. Furthermore, the claim that top-line contraction is irrelevant is contradicted by the -20% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E14], showing structural core revenue decay [E14]. The assertion that foreign institutional ownership offsets promoter weakness [E34] ignores the fact that promoter holdings have collapsed by 12.23 percentage points to a meager 13.70% [E33], flagged explicitly as a low promoter holding risk [E44]. Finally, invoking a discounted cash flow margin of safety [E38] disregards massive underlying balance sheet threats, including Rs 478 Cr in borrowings [E31] and substantial contingent liabilities totaling Rs 415 Cr [E46].
